newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count up 10 to 861 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count up 10 to 861 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 861 as of November 27, up 10 from the prior week and 88 above the year-ago total of 773, Baker Hughes Inc reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by seven to 724, while rigs working offshore rose one to 108. The number of rigs active in inland waters rose by two to 29.
The biggest change in individual states occurred in Texas, which showed an increase of 11 and Pennsylvania, which showed a decrease of three. Michigan rose by three.

A total of 382 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up eight from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by two to 477, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at two.
There were 189 rigs drilling directionally, 64 drilling horizontally and 608 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by eight to 349 versus 240 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
